title: Monomial Rees algebra and affine log blowup chart comparison
statement:
Let $P$ be a fine saturated monoid, written additively, and let $\alpha:P\to(A,\cdot)$ be a chart making $\operatorname{Spec}A$ a locally Noetherian log regular fs log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup, pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $E\subset P$ be finite nonempty, $H=E+P$, $L=\mathbf Z[H]\subset R=\mathbf Z[P]$, and $J=(\alpha(e):e\in E)\subset A$. Here $\mathbf Z[T]$ has basis $z^t$ and multiplication $z^tz^{t'}=z^{t+t'}$. Put $0H=P$ and let $nH$ be the sum of $n$ copies of $H$ for $n>0$. For $h\in E$ put $Q_h=\langle P,e-h\ (e\in E)\rangle\subset P^{\rm gp}$. The canonical maps $A\otimes_R\mathbf Z[nH]\to J^n$, $a\otimes z^p\mapsto a\alpha(p)$, assemble to a graded $A$-algebra isomorphism
$$A\otimes_R\mathcal R_R(L)\simeq\mathcal R_A(J),$$
using the Rees algebra [def-nagata-rees-algebra] and tensor product [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. For every $h\in E$, its degree-zero homogeneous localization at $1\otimes z^ht$ [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero] identifies canonically with both $A\otimes_R\mathbf Z[Q_h]$ and $A[J/\alpha(h)]$ [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring]; the resulting isomorphism sends $a\otimes z^{p-nh}$ to $a\alpha(p)/\alpha(h)^n$ for $p\in nH$. These chart isomorphisms commute with further localizations on pairwise overlaps and identify the underlying scheme of the fine log blowup along the log ideal generated by $E$ with $\operatorname{Bl}_J(\operatorname{Spec}A)$ [lem-trf-coherent-log-ideal-chart-construction, def-nagata-global-blowup].

source.place: Expose VIII, proof of 3.4.6(i), printed p. 111, the two Rees-algebra isomorphisms, using the monomial Tor calculation in the proof of 3.4.3, printed p. 110.

proof.text: For every $n\geq0$, multiplication of monomials shows $L^n=\mathbf Z[nH]$: products of $n$ basis monomials have exponent in $nH$, and every exponent in $nH$ is such a product. For $n=0$ both sides are $R$. The subset $nH$ is a monoid ideal. Apply [lem-trf-log-regular-monomial-tor] to it: $\mu_n:A\otimes_R\mathbf Z[nH]\to A$ is injective with image $(\alpha(p):p\in nH)$. This image is $J^n$, since each $p\in nH$ is $e_1+\cdots+e_n+q$ with $e_i\in E,q\in P$, and products of the $\alpha(e_i)$ generate $J^n$. Thus $\mu_n$ is the asserted isomorphism onto $J^n$; for $n=0$ it is multiplication $A\otimes_R R\to A$.

source.place: Expose VIII, proof of 3.4.6(i), printed p. 111, the two Rees-algebra isomorphisms, using the monomial Tor calculation in the proof of 3.4.3, printed p. 110.

proof.text: Use [def-nagata-rees-algebra] to write a Rees element as a finite sum $\sum_n x_nt^n$, $x_n\in L^n$. The map $a\otimes\sum_n x_nt^n\mapsto\sum_n\mu_n(a\otimes x_n)t^n$ has inverse $\sum_n y_nt^n\mapsto\sum_n\iota_n(\mu_n^{-1}(y_n))$, where $\iota_n(a\otimes x)=a\otimes xt^n$. These maps are defined by the bilinear universal property in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]; the coefficient projections and the inclusions show that both composites are identities on pure tensors and on homogeneous elements. On homogeneous pure tensors multiplication is $\mu_{m+n}(ab\otimes xy)=ab\alpha(xy)=\mu_m(a\otimes x)\mu_n(b\otimes y)$, where $\alpha$ here denotes the ring map $R\to A$. Bilinearity extends the equality to finite sums; the degree-zero unit is preserved. This proves the graded $A$-algebra isomorphism.

source.place: Expose VIII, proof of 3.4.6(i), printed p. 111, the two Rees-algebra isomorphisms, using the monomial Tor calculation in the proof of 3.4.3, printed p. 110.

proof.text: Put $B=\mathcal R_R(L)$ and $f_h=z^ht$. By [def-nagata-homogeneous-localization-degree-zero], $B_{(f_h),0}$ consists of finite sums of $z^pt^n/f_h^n$ with $p\in nH$. Send this monomial fraction to $z^{p-nh}$. Indeed $Q_h=\bigcup_{n\geq0}(nH-nh)$: the union contains $P$ and $e-h$, is closed under addition, and $p=e_1+\cdots+e_n+q$ gives $p-nh=q+\sum_i(e_i-h)$. Any finite sum has a common $n$, by increasing $n$ and adding the same multiple of $h$ to $p$. Since $P\to P^{\rm gp}$ is injective by [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], the basis map $\mathbf Z[P]\to\mathbf Z[P^{\rm gp}]$ is injective, even when $P^{\rm gp}$ has torsion. Shifting exponents by $h$ is injective, so multiplication by $f_h$ is injective in $B$. Equality of two fractions, after a common denominator, is exactly equality of their coefficients on each group exponent. Thus the displayed map and the inverse obtained by choosing $q=p-nh$ are well-defined inverses. Addition and multiplication follow from addition of exponents. We get $B_{(f_h),0}\simeq\mathbf Z[Q_h]$ over $R$.

source.place: Expose VIII, proof of 3.4.6(i), printed p. 111, the two Rees-algebra isomorphisms, using the monomial Tor calculation in the proof of 3.4.3, printed p. 110.

proof.text: Apply [lem-nagata-homogeneous-localization-scalar-extension] with base ring $R$, extension $A$, graded algebra $B$, and degree-one element $f_h$. It identifies $(A\otimes_R B)_{(1\otimes f_h),0}$ with $A\otimes_R B_{(f_h),0}$, hence with $A\otimes_R\mathbf Z[Q_h]$ by step 3. The formula is $a\otimes z^{p-nh}\mapsto(a\otimes z^pt^n)/(1\otimes f_h)^n$. The graded isomorphism of step 2 sends the latter fraction to $a\alpha(p)t^n/(\alpha(h)t)^n$. Now [def-nagata-homogeneous-away-to-chart] defines $\theta_{\alpha(h)}$ by sending this to $a\alpha(p)/\alpha(h)^n$ in $A[J/\alpha(h)]$. Its ring-homomorphism property is [lemma-nagata-homogeneous-away-to-chart], and its injectivity and surjectivity are [lemma-nagata-homogeneous-away-to-chart-injective, lemma-nagata-homogeneous-away-to-chart-surjective]. Thus it is an isomorphism, and the formula on $a\in A$ makes it an $A$-algebra isomorphism. No flatness of $A$ over $R$ has been assumed.

source.place: Expose VIII, proof of 3.4.6(i), printed p. 111, the two Rees-algebra isomorphisms, using the monomial Tor calculation in the proof of 3.4.3, printed p. 110.

proof.text: For $h,k\in E$, the overlap in the $h$ chart inverts $f_k/f_h$, namely $z^{k-h}$ on the monoid side and $\alpha(k)/\alpha(h)$ on the ordinary chart side. The isomorphism in step 4 sends the first to the second. The localization relation of [def-weil-ring-localization-away] therefore extends the map uniquely to the overlap, carrying $u/(z^{k-h})^r$ to $\phi_h(u)/(\alpha(k)/\alpha(h))^r$. For a numerator $z^pt^n$, its image from the $h$ chart in the common localization at $f_hf_k$ is $z^{p+nk}t^{2n}/(f_hf_k)^n$; from the $k$ chart the formula is $z^{p+nh}t^{2n}/(f_hf_k)^n$. Applying the graded map in step 2 gives exactly the corresponding formulas with $z^p$ replaced by $\alpha(p)$. Hence the two chart comparisons commute with the canonical overlap maps. Their identity, inverse and triple compatibility are those of [lemma-nagata-proj-chart-ring-cocycle].

source.place: Expose VIII, proof of 3.4.6(i), printed p. 111, the two Rees-algebra isomorphisms, using the monomial Tor calculation in the proof of 3.4.3, printed p. 110.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-coherent-log-ideal-chart-construction], the fine log blowup is glued from $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R\mathbf Z[Q_h])$ along the common localizations just compared. By [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart-cover], the ordinary blowup is covered by $\operatorname{Spec}(A[J/\alpha(h)])$ for $h\in E$. The standard chart isomorphisms and their overlap identifications are those of [prop-nagata-affine-blowup-chart, lemma-nagata-proj-chart-ring-cocycle]. Step 5 shows the local isomorphisms agree on overlaps. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] to these maps and to their inverses. Their composites restrict to the identity on every chart, so uniqueness in the same gluing theorem makes them identities globally. All chart maps preserve $A$, so the resulting isomorphism is over $\operatorname{Spec}A$. This identifies the underlying scheme of the fine (unsaturated) log blowup with the ordinary blowup as claimed.
